recommendation: Keep the audit commit and have OO explicitly finish FHIR-53307 or a successor by deciding whether current R6 ObservationDefinition.device[x] 0..1 supersedes FHIR-28097, or whether repeating device support should be restored with a publisher-valid non-choice/backbone model.
issue_request: FHIR-28097 asked OO to change ObservationDefinition.device from 0..1 to 0..* and clarify that multiple devices are inclusive OR: observations of this kind use one or more listed devices or models. Jira status is Published with Persuasive resolution for R5.
initial_application: The original application appears in commit 56b91f72c1e36104fa43f12c189891648867d5bd, which applied FHIR-26921, FHIR-28097, FHIR-28096, FHIR-26603, and FHIR-28608 and changed ObservationDefinition.device to max * while adding DeviceDefinition support. There was no prior FHIR-28097 reconcile commit on the combined branch.
additional_context: ObservationDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source defines ObservationDefinition.device[x] as 0..1 with Reference(Device) and canonical(DeviceDefinition). Later FHIR-39389 DeviceDefinition canonical-resource work made DeviceDefinition references canonical, creating the current choice element. FHIR-53307 documents that repeating device[x] violates the publisher rule for choice elements and lists accepting 0..1 or splitting/remodeling as options; OO minutes on 2025-11-07 record a 7-0-0 motion to accept revised 0..1, but the Jira remains Triaged and later comments/minutes continue discussing specific and multiple Device use cases.
reconciliation: Published an empty human-review audit commit. No source change was made because restoring max * on the current device[x] choice would violate publisher rules, while splitting or remodeling the element would decide the still-open FHIR-53307 design question.

related_jiras.note: Companion Published issue added DeviceDefinition as an allowed ObservationDefinition.device target and was applied in the same 2021 source commit.
Later DeviceDefinition canonical-resource modeling changed DeviceDefinition references to canonical(DeviceDefinition), creating the current device[x] choice shape.
R6 cardinality issue documents the choice-element publisher constraint and the choice between accepting 0..1 or remodeling for repeatability, but remains Triaged.
